recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not reintroduce ProcedureStatement or Procedure.asserter for FHIR-12633 without a new Patient Care decision, because the current source matches the published issue disposition plus later approved refinements.
issue_request: FHIR-12633 asked whether Procedure should be split into Procedure and ProcedureStatement for summary procedure statements versus detailed procedure execution records. The final Published/Not Persuasive with Modification disposition kept a single Procedure resource, added Procedure.asserter and Procedure.recorder, and required a scope update for current and historical procedures.
initial_application: Commit edd8a7650ab34c3be2f69f49a42d8e59954e3e2e applied GF#12633 by updating Procedure scope text and adding Procedure.asserter and Procedure.recorder in the then-current Procedure spreadsheet. The current XML source was later reworked/regenerated and preserves Procedure.recorder with a GF#12633 committee note.
additional_context: Procedure remains active in source/fhir.ini, no ProcedureStatement resource exists in current source, and the Procedure narrative says the resource covers current and historical procedures while providing summary-level rather than real-time execution detail. Later Published issue FHIR-19511 renamed/redefined Procedure.asserter as Procedure.reported[x], and source/fhir.ini now maps Procedure.asserter to Procedure.reported[x]. Later Applied issue FHIR-32505 clarified recorder versus reported[x], and that comment is present on Procedure.recorder.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source already satisfies the seed's final decision when later Patient Care decisions are considered: one active Procedure resource, current/historical scope wording, recorder present with the requested reference targets, and reported[x] as the approved successor to asserter.
